summary: This diff fixes two real bugs cleanly: escalate() in veridian-task-watchdog.py now threads the stalled task's own task.yaml repo field through to the RCA escalation's --repo argument (both call sites updated) instead of hardcoding claude-control, with a safe fallback when the task dict is None or missing the field; and cmd_checkpoint() in veridian-task.py now excludes the repo's default branch (resolved via symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD, which is guaranteed present since cmd_create itself relies on it with check=True and it is a shared, not per-worktree, ref) from being trusted as a real @{upstream} branch, correctly root-causing why fresh worktrees created via git worktree add -b <branch> origin/<default> had @{upstream} pointing at the default branch before any real push. I read both modified functions in full, confirmed all call sites were updated consistently, verified the logic against how cmd_create actually constructs worktrees, and ran the test suite (python3 -m pytest tests/veridian_task_branch_resolution_test.py) -- all 6 tests pass, including 3 new regression tests that exercise the real module via importlib against real git repos rather than mocks. No .github/workflows changes, no auth/payment/migration/schema paths touched, no injection risk (subprocess calls use list args, not shell=True), consistent with tier1 classification.
